### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. cardiac-urogenital syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.714)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:1181)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYRF (HGNC:1181) —DISRUPTS→ Regulation of oligodendrocyte differentiation (GO:0007421); Regulation of oligodendrocyte differentiation (GO:0007421) —LEADS_TO→ Dural ectasia (HP:0030047); Regulation of oligodendrocyte differentiation (GO:0007421) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital heart defect (HP:0001627). Loss-of-function mutations in MYRF disrupt the regulation of oligodendrocyte differentiation, which is implicated in both dural ectasia (a feature of MONDO:0010836) and congenital heart defects (a feature of cardiac-urogenital syndrome).

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic loss-of-function variants in MYRF are not observed in patients with MONDO:0010836 or cardiac-urogenital syndrome, or if gain-of-function variants are found to cause one of the diseases while loss-of-function causes the other, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.1%) in MYRF with a predicted deleterious effect.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYRF in these two conditions could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting oligodendrocyte differentiation pathways for both neurological and cardiac developmental disorders.

#### 2. encephalitis/encephalopathy, mild, with reversible myelin vacuolization  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.712)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:1181)

**Proposed mechanism:** MYRF (HGNC:1181) —DISRUPTS→ Myelin sheath formation and maintenance (GO:0048714); Myelin sheath formation and maintenance (GO:0048714) —LEADS_TO→ Dysmyelination (HP:0003300); Myelin sheath formation and maintenance (GO:0048714) —LEADS_TO→ Encephalopathy (HP:0012298); Myelin sheath formation and maintenance (GO:0048714) —LEADS_TO→ Vacuolization of myelin (HP:0033633). Loss-of-function mutations in MYRF disrupt the process of myelin sheath formation and maintenance, leading to dysmyelination, encephalopathy, and vacuolization of myelin, which are characteristic phenotypes of both MONDO:0010836 and MONDO:0020853.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in MYRF in individuals with MONDO:0010836 that do not impair myelin sheath formation or maintenance, or the absence of MYRF variants in individuals with MONDO:0020853. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing common variants in MYRF that are not associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MYRF in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies for myelin disorders, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
